'''''Cosmos parviflorus''''', commonly known as the '''southwestern cosmos''', is an [[annual plant|annual]], [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]], [[flowering plant]] in the [[Asteraceae]] family. It is native to parts of the [[Southwestern United States]] and most of  [[Mexico]] (from [[Chihuahua (state)|Chihuahua]] to [[Oaxaca]]) and appears to be introduced in portions of the [[Northeastern United States]] ([[Maryland]], [[Maine]], [[Rhode Island]] and [[Massachusetts]]).

==Description==
''Cosmos parviflorus'' is an annual, herbaceous, flowering plant that typically grows between {{cvt|30|and|90|cm|in}} tall. The [[opposite leaf|opposite]] leaves are attached to [[leaf petiole|petioles]] around 0.5 cm long, and are deeply divided into narrow [[linear leaf|linear]] segments. The [[ray florets]] are a white, pink or violet color with the colors sometimes mixed in the same population. The [[achenes]] are barbed, causing them to lodge in fur or clothing. They can thus be transported over long distances.<ref>Wiggins. Vegetation and Flora of the Sonoran Desert. Stanford University Press, 1964</ref><ref name=":FNA" />

The plant typically flowers from July to October.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=SEINet Portal Network - Cosmos parviflorus |url=https://swbiodiversity.org/seinet/taxa/index.php?taxon=3600 |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=swbiodiversity.org}}</ref><ref name=":FNA" />

==Distribution and habitat==

''Cosmos parviflorus'' is native to Mexico (from Chihuahua to Oaxaca) and parts of the [[United States]] ([[Texas]], [[New Mexico]], [[Arizona]], [[Colorado]]). Collections of this species have also been made in [[Missouri]], Maryland, Massachusetts, Maine and Rhode Island, though it appears that this species is not native in those states.<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Cosmos%20parviflorus.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Tropicos |url=https://www.tropicos.org/Name/50043387?tab=specimens |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=www.tropicos.org}}</ref><ref>García-Mendoza, A. J. & J. A. Meave. 2011. Diversidad Florística de Oaxaca: de Musgos a Angispermas 1–351. Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, Ciudad Universitaria</ref>

=== Habitat ===
This species grows in open or forested slopes and canyons at elevations of 100 to 3000 meters from [[sea level]]. It also is a common weed in agricultural fields.<ref name=":FNA">{{Cite web |title=Cosmos parviflorus - FNA |url=http://floranorthamerica.org/Cosmos_parviflorus |access-date=1 December 2024 |website=Flora of North America}}</ref>

==Conservation==
{{As of|2024|December}}, the conservation group [[NatureServe]] listed ''Cosmos parviflorus'' as [[NatureServe conservation status|Secure (G5)]] worldwide. This status was last reviewed on 11 June 1993.<ref name=":NS" />

==Taxonony==
''Cosmos parviflorus'' was first named as ''Coreopsis parviflora'' by [[Nicolaus Jacquin]] in 1798. In 1807, [[Christiaan Hendrik Persoon]] renamed the species to its currently accepted name, ''Cosmos parviflorus''.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Cosmos parviflorus (Jacq.) Pers. | Plants of the World Online | Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:198352-1 |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

=== Etymology ===
The [[specific name (botany)|species epithet]] ''parviflorus'' means "small-flowered". In English, the plant is commonly called the '''southwestern cosmos'''.<ref name=":1" />
